name: equal_angle_pair_carry_doubling
precondition: family dv_angle; needs nonclifford_rz and ancilla_room; min_qubits 2, max_qubits 20. Fires only if, among the OFF-GRID rotations of the circuit (rotation(op) not None and not on_grid(theta)), there exist at least two with the same |theta| whose doubled angle IS on the grid, i.e. on_grid(2*|theta|). This is a two-rotation condition only - no multiplicity 3 or more is required, no Hadamard-free locality is required. qft_8 satisfies it: the angle histogram has |theta| = pi/8 with multiplicity 6 (2*pi/8 = pi/4, on grid) and |theta| = 3pi/8 with multiplicity 2 (2*3pi/8 = 3pi/4, on grid), out of 33 off-grid rotations.
identity: Take exactly TWO rotations of equal angle theta about commuting Paulis P1, P2, with on_grid(2*theta). Copy each Pauli's eigenvalue bit to a clean ancilla by a CNOT ladder over its support (local Cliffords first if the Pauli is X/Y-type), giving bits x1 on a1 and x2 on a2, so the pair becomes Rz(theta)_{a1} Rz(theta)_{a2}. Then: (i) and_compute(a1, a2) -> fresh ancilla c = x1 AND x2 (4 T, exact); (ii) CNOT a1 -> a2, so a2 now holds s = x1 XOR x2; (iii) apply Rz(-theta) on a2 and Rz(-2*theta) on c - the second is a multiple of pi/4, so with_ops lowers it to Clifford/T and gridsynth pays NOTHING for it; (iv) CNOT a1 -> a2 again (restores x2), and_uncompute(c) (0 T: X-basis measurement + classically controlled CZ), then undo the parity ladders. Two off-grid rotations become ONE off-grid rotation plus one grid rotation plus one AND gadget. The saving is purely an ANGLE-COST saving: the gate count does not fall, the second rotation's angle is MOVED onto the pi/4 grid by the carry bit of x1+x2, where it is free. This is not angle snapping (no angle is perturbed, error is exactly zero), not phase folding (the two axes are different and do not merge), and not a phase-gradient construction (no catalyst register, no shared resource state, nothing amortized across the circuit). It differs from Hamming-weight phasing over k >= 3 equal-angle rotations in the one way that matters to this runner: a pair match is SELF-CONTAINED and lowers T on its own, so it survives the runner's one-match-at-a-time pricing, whereas any construction with a one-time preparation cost is priced against a single rotation's saving and dropped.
correctness: Rz(theta) = diag(e^{-i theta/2}, e^{i theta/2}) = e^{-i theta/2} diag(1, e^{i theta}), so on bits x1, x2 the pair equals e^{-i theta} e^{i theta (x1 + x2)} up to global phase. For bits, x1 + x2 = (x1 XOR x2) + 2 (x1 AND x2) exactly, hence e^{i theta (x1+x2)} = e^{i theta s} * e^{i 2 theta c} with s = x1 XOR x2 and c = x1 AND x2. Each factor is diagonal in a computational-basis bit, and e^{i theta b} = e^{i theta/2} Rz(-theta) on the wire holding b, so the product is Rz(-theta) on the s wire times Rz(-2 theta) on the c wire, up to global phase (invariant 6). Validity of treating the two rotations as acting simultaneously: P1 and P2 commute (checked by the trigger via pauli.commutes on pauli.frames records) and each commutes with the Pauli of every rotation record positioned between them, so both exponentials slide to one common slice; the Clifford ops in between are absorbed exactly by the frame sweep (pauli.frames / residual_clifford). Parity copy: CNOTs from the support of P_i onto a clean ancilla a_i leave the data invariant and conjugate Z_{a_i} to P_i exactly; the ladder is its own inverse, so a1, a2 return to |0> after the undo. and_compute/and_uncompute is Gidney's temporary AND: exact, and its uncompute is an X-basis measurement with a classically controlled CZ, so on EVERY measurement branch the Kraus operator is the SAME unitary times the same scalar and c is returned to |0> deterministically - precisely what the judge's branch-wise specification check tests (invariant 2). Total error introduced: zero; the surviving rotations are unchanged in angle, and there are fewer of them, so eps_rz = eps_synth / N_Rz grows and the remaining ones also get slightly cheaper.
trigger: Run pauli.frames(ops) -> Records(pos, theta, x, z, sign, on_grid); drop records with on_grid. Normalize sign into the Pauli: (theta < 0, P) -> (|theta|, -P). Bucket by |theta| to 1e-9 and keep only buckets whose angle satisfies dv.on_grid(2*|theta|). Within such a bucket, scan positions in order and greedily take DISJOINT pairs (i, j), i < j, such that (a) pauli.commutes(P_i, P_j), (b) P_i commutes with the Pauli of every off-grid rotation record whose pos lies strictly between pos_i and pos_j, and (c) weight(P_i) + weight(P_j) <= 6 so the parity ladders stay small. Emit one match per surviving pair, carrying the two record positions, the common slice (pos_j), and 3 clean ancillas requested with append_ancillas (reused across matches, so at most 3 are live at once). Emit nothing for a bucket where no pair passes - an empty bucket costs nothing. On qft_8 this emits at most 3 pairs at pi/8 and 1 pair at 3pi/8.
expected_effect: Each accepted pair deletes two off-grid rotations and inserts one off-grid rotation of the same angle plus one pi/4-grid rotation (free, or 1-3 explicit T) plus one and_compute (4 T) and one and_uncompute (0 T). At eps_rz = 3.03e-5 an off-grid rotation costs ~47.6 T (33 of them buy 1572 of the current 1583), so each pair nets about 47.6 - 5 ~ 42 T. Four pairs (three at pi/8, one at 3pi/8) take the off-grid count 33 -> 29 for ~170 T, and the resulting eps_rz rescaling (eps_synth/29 instead of /33) shaves roughly another 3*log2(33/29)*29 ~ 16 T off the survivors: 1583 -> about 1400 on 11 qubits (8 data + 3 reusable ancillas), against DPF Synth's 1064 on 34. Scored conservatively at the value of the pi/8 bucket alone, in case the betweenness guard in (b) kills the 3pi/8 pair and one pi/8 pair.
source: Carry/parity decomposition of equal-angle phasing: I. D. Kivlichan, C. Gidney, D. W. Berry, N. Wiebe, J. McClean, W. Sun, Z. Jiang, N. Rubin, A. Fowler, A. Aspuru-Guzik, H. Neven, R. Babbush, 'Improved Fault-Tolerant Quantum Simulation of Condensed-Phase Correlated Electrons via Trotterization', Quantum 4, 296 (2020), 'Hamming weight phasing' (specialized here to the k = 2 carry, where the doubled angle lands on the Clifford+T grid); temporary-AND gadget from C. Gidney, 'Halving the cost of quantum addition', Quantum 2, 74 (2018).
